concepts.name: IMF Founding, Mandate and Bretton Woods Origins
key_dimensions: Distinction between IMF and World Bank mandates at Bretton Woods (1944) — common UPSC trap of conflating the two
IMF's core purposes: exchange rate stability, balance of payments adjustment, international monetary cooperation
Shift from Bretton Woods fixed-exchange-rate system (1971 Nixon Shock) and IMF's evolving role post-collapse
Difference between IMF Articles of Agreement and IBRD Articles — overlapping but distinct legal foundations

concepts.name: IMF Quota System: Structure, Calculation and Implications
key_dimensions: What quota determines: voting power, subscription contribution, access to IMF financing, and SDR allocation — all four linkages are individually testable
Quota formula variables (GDP, openness, variability, reserves) and the controversy over under-representation of EMEs
2010 Quota and Governance Reform (effective 2016): shift of >6% quota shares to EMEs, India's revised ranking
UPSC trap: quota is NOT solely based on GDP; the multi-variable formula is frequently misrepresented

concepts.name: IMF Voting Structure and Governance Bodies
key_dimensions: Three-tier governance: Board of Governors → Executive Board (24 EDs) → Managing Director; roles and composition distinctions
Basic votes vs. quota-based votes: basic votes prevent complete domination by large economies — an often-ignored dimension
US veto power: 85% supermajority threshold for major decisions + US ~17% quota = effective veto
UPSC trap: IMF is NOT one-country-one-vote (unlike UN General Assembly); voting is weighted

concepts.name: Special Drawing Rights (SDR): Nature, Valuation and Allocation
key_dimensions: SDR is NOT a currency — it is an international reserve asset and a claim on freely usable currencies of IMF members
SDR basket composition (USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP) and criteria for inclusion (freely usable + export share)
Chinese Yuan inclusion in SDR basket (2016): significance for RMB internationalisation and implications for India
General SDR allocations vs. special allocations; 2021 COVID-19 SDR allocation of $650 billion — largest in IMF history

concepts.name: IMF Lending Facilities: Types, Conditionality and Differences
key_dimensions: Stand-By Arrangement (SBA) vs. Extended Fund Facility (EFF) vs. Flexible Credit Line (FCL) — eligibility and conditionality differences
Concessional facilities for Low-Income Countries (LICs): PRGT (Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust) — Rapid Credit Facility, Extended Credit Facility
Precautionary and Liquidity Line (PLL) vs. FCL: both are precautionary but FCL has no ex-post conditionality — a classic UPSC distinction
Conditionality principle: structural benchmarks vs. performance criteria — why conditionality is politically controversial

concepts.name: IMF's Balance of Payments Surveillance and Article IV Consultations
key_dimensions: Article IV of IMF Articles of Agreement: bilateral surveillance obligation — mandatory annual consultations with member states
Distinction between bilateral surveillance (Article IV), multilateral surveillance (WEO, GFSR) and financial sector surveillance (FSAP)
Currency manipulation clause: IMF's role in flagging 'fundamental exchange rate misalignment' — relevant to US-China and India-US tensions
UPSC trap: Article IV consultations are NOT binding on member states; IMF has no enforcement power over exchange rate policies

concepts.name: IMF and Exchange Rate Regimes
key_dimensions: Evolution from par value system (Bretton Woods) to post-1973 managed float — IMF's role in each phase
IMF de facto classification of exchange rate arrangements (8 categories from hard peg to free float)
India's exchange rate regime classification: managed float — RBI interventions and IMF's monitoring role
UPSC trap: IMF does NOT prescribe a specific exchange rate regime to members post-1978 (Second Amendment); members have choice

concepts.name: IMF Conditionality and Structural Adjustment Programs (SAPs)
key_dimensions: Washington Consensus principles embedded in SAP conditionality: fiscal austerity, privatisation, liberalisation — criticism vs. defence
India's 1991 IMF loan and conditionalities: linkage to LPG reforms — frequently asked in UPSC Mains context
Post-2008 shift in IMF approach: acceptance of capital controls and social spending floors — ideological evolution
Distinction between prior actions, structural benchmarks, and performance criteria in IMF program design

concepts.name: IMF's Role in Global Financial Crises
key_dimensions: Asian Financial Crisis (1997-98): IMF's controversial austerity prescriptions vs. Malaysia's capital controls — competing models
Global Financial Crisis (2008-09): IMF's expanded mandate, G20 coordination, tripling of resources
European Debt Crisis (2010-12): IMF's role in Troika (IMF + ECB + European Commission) — deviation from standard LIC-focused role
COVID-19 response: Catastrophe Containment and Relief Trust (CCRT), SDR allocation, Resilience and Sustainability Trust (RST)

concepts.name: IMF Resources: Funding Mechanisms Beyond Quotas
key_dimensions: New Arrangements to Borrow (NAB): a secondary line of credit from member countries — distinct from quotas
Bilateral Borrowing Agreements (BBAs): third layer of IMF resources — used extensively post-2008
Gold holdings of IMF: IMF is one of largest official holders; restrictions on gold sales under Articles of Agreement
UPSC trap: IMF's primary resource is quota subscriptions, NOT borrowing; the three-layer resource structure is frequently tested

concepts.name: IMF Quota Reforms and Emerging Economy Representation
key_dimensions: 2010 Seoul Quota Reform (effective 2016): BRICS countries among top 10 shareholders post-reform — India's position
Ongoing 16th General Review of Quotas: demand for further realignment toward EMEs and developing countries
Contrast between IMF quota reform (slow, US-blocked for years) and AIIB/NDB as alternative institutions
UPSC trap: the 2010 reform doubled overall quota size AND shifted shares — both dimensions matter, not just share shift

concepts.name: IMF and Low-Income Countries (LICs): Concessional Support
key_dimensions: Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust (PRGT): the umbrella for all concessional lending — funded separately from General Resources Account
Zero-interest rate policy for LIC facilities during crises (waived during COVID-19)
Debt Sustainability Framework (DSF) jointly operated by IMF and World Bank for LICs
UPSC trap: PRGT interest rates are NOT the same as market-rate IMF lending — LICs get subsidised rates, a common confusion

concepts.name: IMF World Economic Outlook (WEO) and Global Financial Stability Report (GFSR)
key_dimensions: WEO: published twice yearly (April, October) + interim updates; covers growth, inflation, trade forecasts — multilateral surveillance tool
GFSR: published by Monetary and Capital Markets Department; focuses on financial system vulnerabilities, not real economy
Fiscal Monitor: third flagship publication — focuses on public finances; the trio (WEO + GFSR + FM) released simultaneously during Spring/Annual Meetings
UPSC trap: WEO forecasts are NOT binding; they are analytical assessments — members frequently contest IMF projections

concepts.name: Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP)
key_dimensions: FSAP: joint IMF-World Bank program assessing financial system stability and development — mandatory for 29 systemically important countries
Two components: Financial System Stability Assessment (FSSA) by IMF + Financial Sector Development assessment by World Bank
India's FSAP assessments and findings on banking sector vulnerabilities — relevant to NPA crisis discourse
UPSC trap: FSAP is mandatory only for systemically important jurisdictions (G-SIFIs host countries); not all IMF members

concepts.name: IMF Managing Director: Selection, Role and Controversies
key_dimensions: Gentlemen's agreement: European heads IMF, American heads World Bank — increasingly challenged post-2008
Managing Director vs. Deputy MDs: first Deputy MD traditionally American — the informal power-sharing arrangement
IMF's role during Dominique Strauss-Kahn controversy (2011) and succession — institutional resilience test
Kristalina Georgieva controversy (2021): World Bank data manipulation allegation — IMF Board's handling and governance implications

concepts.name: IMF and Capital Account Liberalisation
key_dimensions: Original Articles of Agreement: IMF has NO jurisdiction over capital account transactions (only current account) — a fundamental but frequently confused point
IMF's Institutional View (2012) on capital flows: cautious endorsement of capital flow management measures under certain conditions
India's capital account: partially convertible — IMF's position vs. India's gradual approach
UPSC trap: IMF CANNOT require capital account liberalisation as a condition — its mandate is current account convertibility under Article VIII

concepts.name: IMF Article VIII vs. Article XIV: Currency Convertibility Obligations
key_dimensions: Article VIII: full current account convertibility — no restrictions on payments for current international transactions; India accepted in 1994
Article XIV: transitional arrangements allowing restrictions — used by countries not yet ready for full convertibility
Implications of Article VIII acceptance: India cannot reimpose current account restrictions without IMF approval
UPSC trap: Article VIII acceptance does NOT imply capital account convertibility — the two are categorically distinct

concepts.name: IMF and Sovereign Debt Restructuring
key_dimensions: IMF's 'Lending into Arrears' policy: IMF can lend even when a country is in default to private creditors — controversial but important
Sovereign Debt Restructuring Mechanism (SDRM) proposal (2002): Anne Krueger's initiative, rejected by US and financial markets
Common Framework for Debt Treatment (G20+Paris Club+IMF): post-COVID mechanism for LIC debt — IMF's coordinating role
UPSC trap: IMF has NO formal bankruptcy mechanism for sovereigns unlike domestic insolvency law — SDRM was proposed but never adopted

concepts.name: IMF, India and Recent Engagements
key_dimensions: India's quota share and voting power post-2016 reform: ~2.75% quota, ~2.63% voting power — 8th largest shareholder
India's use of IMF resources: last major borrowing was 1991; India is now a net creditor to IMF through NAB
IMF's recommendations on India: fiscal consolidation, banking sector reforms, labour market flexibility — UPSC Mains policy angle
India's position on SDR allocation and IMF governance reforms at G20 — multilateral diplomacy dimension

concepts.name: IMF vs. World Bank vs. BIS: Institutional Distinctions
key_dimensions: IMF: monetary/macroeconomic stability, BoP support, short-to-medium term — vs. World Bank: long-term development finance
BIS (Bank for International Settlements): central bank for central banks, NOT a UN-affiliated body unlike IMF/WB — frequent UPSC trap
IMF vs. regional financial arrangements (CMIM, ESM, BRICS CRA): complementarity vs. competition — IMF delink conditions
UPSC trap: IMF is a UN specialised agency; BIS is NOT — and IMF headquarters is Washington DC, BIS is Basel
